text:
sahil: FYI customer AcmeFinance reporting a big throughput drop on their Dedicated pool since ~08:30 UTC. Latency jumped from ~120ms/token to 900-2kms/token and customer sees request timeouts. They say they didn't change anything on their side.

ops-bot: [alert] Dedicated pool dp-acme-03: aggregate p50 token latency increased 7x, drop in tokens/sec observed at 2026-03-17T08:29:40Z.

maria: @sahil can you paste the pool config? curious about batching params / max_batch_tokens / prefill windows.

sahil: grabbed from console: `pool: dp-acme-03, model: redwood-large-v2, max_batch_tokens: 512, batch_window_ms: 12, prefill_timeout_ms: 50, autoscale: enabled (min:2 max:16)`

lee: interesting — model profile expects avg sequence ~1500 tokens for this customer, max_batch_tokens=512 will force a lot of micro-batches. Could explain throughput collapse.

jess: I also see queue depth oscillation on that pool. small batches + long kv-cache warmups = poor packing. grabbing logs now.

jess: logs (excerpt):
```
[08:29:37] queue.len=312 inflight=18 batching:avg_batch_tokens=420 avg_batch_size=1 avg_wait_ms=14
[08:29:38] schedule: prefilling=true prefill_misses=43 prefill_wait_ms=52
[08:29:39] node-7 GPU util=22% memory=78%
[08:29:39] rpc: throttle=0 but token_throughput=8/s
```

maria: avg_batch_size=1 and avg_batch_tokens=420 suggests requests are single-request but large sequence. the scheduler is refusing to pack because max_batch_tokens is too low and it thinks it would exceed the limit.

lee: Also autoscaler added a node at 08:20 but it didn't help because small batches don't improve GPU utilization. This is noisy-churny behavior — scheduler creates many microbatches instead of waiting slightly longer to pack.

sahil: Customer also sent some sample requests. They are sending long prompts + long expected completions. I asked them to run a repro curl against our staging endpoint and share headers.

jess: quick repro I ran against the pool with similar sized payloads:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v2","prompt":"<1500 tokens>...","max_new_tokens":512, "stream":false}' | jq '.latency'
# result: 1.8s per token average when batch packing disabled
```

maria: proposed mitigation: increase `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 for this pool OR enable token-based batching fallback so multiple short requests with long sequences pack together. also increase `batch_window_ms` from 12 -> 30 to allow packing to form.

lee: + tune prefill: prefill_timeout_ms 50 -> 20 to reduce prefill misses. that should lower prefill overhead on long-seq requests.

sahil: can we do a quick config push to a canary node in that pool? want to test on node-7 first.

jess: doing canary: applying: `max_batch_tokens=4096, batch_window_ms=30, prefill_timeout_ms=20` to node-7 only. restarting batcher service on node-7 now.

ops-bot: [deploy] batcher-config-change applied to node-7 (canary) by jess at 2026-03-17T08:46:12Z

jess: node-7 coming up. early telemetry: avg_batch_size -> 3, avg_batch_tokens -> 1400, gpu util -> 68%

maria: nice. any impact on latency?

jess: p50 token latency on node-7 dropped from 860ms -> 220ms. tokens/sec increased ~3.6x on that node.

sahil: pinged AcmeFinance — asked if they'd like us to roll the config to rest of pool. they said yes, urgent.

lee: before rolling cluster-wide let's add a guard: set `max_batch_tokens` per model-profile to protect tiny-model tenants. and add a new metric alert for avg_batch_size<1.5 + gpu_util<30% across pool.

maria: also filing a follow-up to engineering: scheduler should consider wait-time vs token-limit tradeoff rather than only token budget. i.e., allow brief additional wait to achieve >=2 requests per batch when sequences are long.

jess: rolled config to all nodes in dp-acme-03. restart wave 1/4 done. no errors.

ops-bot: [info] roll update: dp-acme-03 batcher-config updated across 5 nodes between 2026-03-17T08:52:00Z - 2026-03-17T09:01:10Z

jess: post-roll telemetry: pool avg_batch_size=2.7 avg_batch_tokens=1320 gpu_util=61% tokens/sec +320% p50 token latency -> ~210ms

sahil: customer confirms request latency back to normal and they saw dropped timeouts cleared. customer thanks + asked for RCA.

maria: RCA notes (quick): root cause = pool-level batching config (max_batch_tokens=512) mismatched to workload with long sequences; scheduler default packing policy prioritized token limit over short additional wait causing micro-batches; autoscaler scaled but small batches kept GPU underutilized. mitigation = raised max_batch_tokens, increased batch_window_ms, reduced prefill timeout; added model-profile guard and scheduler change request.

lee: created ticket INF-4923 to track scheduler heuristic change + alert addition.

sahil: moving customer to postmortem thread & sending summary. thanks team :thumbsup:

jess: marking this thread resolved.
